dedupe_keys.name: seismic multi hazard risk and restoration of the tehran sari railway

description: This study develops an integrated probabilistic model of seismic multi-hazard risk and restoration for railway networks and applies it to the Tehran-Sari railway in Iran, a mountain line linking the capital with the Caspian coast. Saeideh Farahani, Ali Shojaeian, Behrouz Behnam and Milad Roohi of Amirkabir University of Technology and US universities published it in Sustainable and Resilient Infrastructure in 2023. The model accounts for ground shaking from seismic wave propagation, liquefaction and landslides, the main phenomena that damage distributed networks, through a GIS-based user interface, and computes combined damage states of network components, component and system functionality, restoration over time and economic loss. The case study shows the method can quantify these physical and economic metrics to help officials plan retrofits that reduce loss and improve the resilience of railway segments. Coverage: one railway line. Access: article, open access. Licence and cost: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, free. Caveats: fragility and restoration functions appear to come from the literature, not local data, and the tool itself is not released. It supports hazard exposure, network functionality and restoration modelling of rail lines in seismic regions. It follows the component fragility and restoration logic of HAZUS, which is catalogued here.
